title: Pressure-Volume-Temperature-Concentration Relation of Aqueous Sodium Chloride Solutions (A. M. Rowe Jr., J. C. S. Chou)
experimental_method: Differential change of specific volume with pressure measured in a stainless steel vessel with a calibrated positive-displacement pump (piston displacement with test-vessel valve open and closed per 250 psi step), corrected for vessel dilation; derivative values from the mean volume change per small pressure step.
uncertainties_stated: Pressure gauge +-3 psi; temperature +-0.1 C after calibration (potentiometer precision +-0.02 C); replicate variation of mean piston displacement within 0.5 percent; fitted formula deviates less than 1.5 ppt from the observations.
quality_remarks: PDF page 1 begins with the references and acknowledgement of another article (hard-sphere/virial paper); Rowe and Chou start on PDF page 2. Values at 21.7 C disagree with derivatives calculated from sound velocity, increasingly with NaCl concentration (authors' own comparison). Table II (mean compressibility at 0 C by authors' equations and by Tait's formula) is calculated, not extracted. The measured quantity is a pressure derivative of volume, not density. Temperature scale not stated.
not_extracted_tables: Table II (mean compressibility at 0 C computed from the authors' interpolation formula and from Tait's formula; derived and literature)
density/P-v-T-x interpolation formula and its coefficients (fitted)
